text: Dogs cool down mainly by panting.
explanation: Dogs sweat a little through their paw pads, but that is not enough to cool the body. Panting is their main way to release heat.

text: A wagging tail always means a dog is happy.
explanation: Tail wagging shows that a dog is emotionally aroused. A stiff, high wag can mean the dog is tense or unsure, so look at the whole body.

text: Dogs see the world only in black and white.
explanation: Dogs see colors, just fewer than we do. They see mostly blues and yellows and have trouble telling red from green.

text: Chocolate is toxic to dogs.
explanation: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs break down very slowly. Dark chocolate and cocoa powder are the most dangerous.

text: One dog year always equals seven human years.
explanation: Dogs grow up very fast in their first two years, and then aging depends on size. Large breeds usually age faster than small ones.

text: A warm, dry nose means a dog is sick.
explanation: A dog's nose can be warm or dry many times a day, for example after a nap. Appetite, energy and behavior tell you much more.

text: Grapes and raisins can be dangerous for dogs.
explanation: Grapes and raisins can cause kidney failure in dogs, and even a small amount can be harmful. Keep them out of reach.

text: Older dogs cannot learn new tricks.
explanation: Dogs can learn at any age. Senior dogs may need shorter sessions, but they enjoy training with treats and praise.

text: A dog's sense of smell is many times stronger than a human's.
explanation: Dogs have hundreds of millions of scent receptors, while humans have only a few million. That is why dogs can find people and detect tiny traces of smells.

text: Most dogs in shelters are there because of bad behavior.
explanation: Common reasons are owners moving, housing rules, money problems or other life changes. Many shelter dogs are already house-trained and friendly.

text: Puppies are born with their eyes closed.
explanation: Puppies are born blind and deaf. Their eyes usually open when they are about 10 to 14 days old.

text: Dogs need a bath every day to stay clean.
explanation: Bathing too often removes the natural oils that protect a dog's skin and coat. Most dogs need a bath only every few weeks or when they get dirty.

text: Xylitol, a sweetener in some sugar-free gum, is dangerous for dogs.
explanation: Xylitol can cause a sudden drop in a dog's blood sugar and even liver damage. Always check labels on sugar-free products.

text: Dogs eat grass only when they feel sick.
explanation: Many healthy dogs eat grass, and most of them do not vomit afterwards. It is a common and usually harmless behavior.

text: An adult dog has 42 teeth.
explanation: Adult dogs have 42 permanent teeth. Puppies have 28 baby teeth, which fall out at around 3 to 6 months of age.

text: Dogs can understand when a person points at something.
explanation: Many dogs, even young puppies, can follow a pointing hand to find hidden food. It shows how closely dogs have learned to work with people.

text: Cats always land on their feet.
explanation: Cats have a righting reflex that helps them turn in the air, but they can still be badly hurt in falls. Secure windows and balconies.

text: Milk is a healthy treat for adult cats.
explanation: Many adult cats are lactose intolerant, so milk can upset their stomach. Fresh water is the best drink for a cat.

text: Cats purr only when they are happy.
explanation: Cats also purr when they are stressed, unwell or in pain. Purring can be a way to calm themselves down.

text: Cats often sleep 12 to 16 hours a day.
explanation: Cats are natural hunters that save energy by sleeping a lot. Kittens and senior cats may sleep even more.

text: Lilies are highly toxic to cats.
explanation: Even a small amount of a lily, including its pollen or the water from the vase, can cause kidney failure in cats.

text: Cats cannot be trained.
explanation: Cats can learn their name, tricks and using a scratching post. Rewards like treats and play work best.

text: Cats cannot taste sweet flavors.
explanation: Cats lack a working sweet taste receptor. As meat eaters, they do not need to detect sugar.

text: Indoor cats do not need any vaccinations.
explanation: Some viruses can be brought inside on shoes or clothes, and indoor cats sometimes escape. Vets still recommend core vaccines.

text: Cats have a third eyelid.
explanation: The third eyelid, called the nictitating membrane, protects and moistens the eye. You usually only see it when a cat is sleepy or unwell.

text: Cats never need company or attention.
explanation: Many cats bond strongly with their people and get bored or stressed without play and interaction.

text: Kittens are usually ready for a new home at around 8 to 12 weeks old.
explanation: In the first weeks, kittens learn important social skills from their mother and littermates. Leaving too early can cause behavior problems.

text: Cats can stay healthy on a vegan diet.
explanation: Cats are obligate carnivores. They need nutrients from animal tissue, such as taurine, to keep their heart and eyes healthy.

text: Declawing a cat is just like trimming its nails.
explanation: Declawing removes the last bone of each toe. It is painful, and many countries ban or strongly discourage it.

text: All cats hate water.
explanation: Many cats dislike getting wet, but some, for example many Turkish Vans, enjoy playing with water.

text: An adult cat has 30 teeth.
explanation: Adult cats have 30 permanent teeth. Kittens have 26 baby teeth.

text: Whiskers help cats sense the world around them.
explanation: Whiskers are very sensitive to touch and air movement. They help cats move in the dark and sense nearby objects, so never cut them.

text: Carrots should be the main food in a rabbit's diet.
explanation: Carrots are high in sugar, so they are only an occasional treat. Most of a rabbit's diet should be hay, plus some leafy greens.

text: A rabbit's teeth never stop growing.
explanation: Rabbit teeth grow all their life. Chewing lots of hay keeps them at a healthy length.

text: Rabbits are rodents.
explanation: Rabbits are lagomorphs, not rodents. One difference is that rabbits have a second, small pair of upper front teeth.

text: Rabbits can be litter-trained.
explanation: Rabbits naturally choose one place for their toilet, so most of them learn to use a litter box quickly.

text: Rabbits are easy, low-care pets for small children.
explanation: Rabbits are fragile, often dislike being picked up, need daily exercise and can live for many years. They are a big commitment.

text: Rabbits eat some of their own droppings.
explanation: Rabbits eat special soft droppings called cecotropes. They are full of nutrients and are an important part of healthy digestion.

text: Rabbits can vomit if they eat something bad.
explanation: Rabbits cannot vomit. That is why it is so important to keep harmful foods and plants away from them.

text: Happy rabbits sometimes jump and twist in the air.
explanation: This happy jump is called a binky. It is a sign that a rabbit feels safe and playful.

text: It is fine to pick up a rabbit by its ears.
explanation: Lifting a rabbit by its ears is painful and can injure it. Support the chest and the back legs when you hold a rabbit.

text: Pet rabbits can live 8 to 12 years.
explanation: With good food, care and vet visits, pet rabbits often live 8 to 12 years, so adopting one is a long-term decision.

text: Rabbits are happy living alone in a small hutch.
explanation: Rabbits are social animals that need space to run every day. Many are happiest with another rabbit as a friend.

text: Rabbits can see almost all the way around themselves.
explanation: Their eyes are on the sides of their head, which helps them spot danger. They have only a small blind spot right in front of the nose.

text: Iceberg lettuce is a great everyday food for rabbits.
explanation: Iceberg lettuce has very little nutrition and can upset a rabbit's stomach. Darker leafy greens are a better choice.

text: Rabbits are most active at dawn and dusk.
explanation: Rabbits are crepuscular. They are usually most lively early in the morning and in the evening.

text: A rabbit that stops eating needs a vet quickly.
explanation: If a rabbit stops eating, its gut can slow down or stop, and this can become life-threatening fast. Call a vet the same day.

text: Guinea pigs come from Guinea in Africa.
explanation: Guinea pigs come from the Andes region of South America, where people domesticated them thousands of years ago.

text: Guinea pigs need vitamin C from their food.
explanation: Just like humans, guinea pigs cannot make their own vitamin C. Without it in their diet, they can get scurvy.

text: Guinea pigs are happiest living alone.
explanation: Guinea pigs are herd animals and get lonely on their own. It is best to keep at least two together.

text: A guinea pig's teeth never stop growing.
explanation: Their teeth grow all their life. Unlimited hay helps wear them down naturally.

text: When a guinea pig jumps straight up in the air, it is usually happy.
explanation: This jump is called popcorning. It is most common in young guinea pigs and shows excitement and joy.

text: Guinea pigs and rabbits can share a cage without any problems.
explanation: They need different diets, a rabbit can hurt a guinea pig by accident, and rabbits can carry bacteria that make guinea pigs sick.

text: Guinea pigs live only 1 to 2 years.
explanation: Guinea pigs usually live 5 to 7 years, and some live even longer with good care.

text: Baby guinea pigs are born with fur and open eyes.
explanation: Baby guinea pigs are very developed at birth. They can run around and start nibbling solid food within days.

text: Guinea pigs need an exercise wheel, like hamsters.
explanation: Wheels can hurt a guinea pig's back and legs. They need plenty of floor space to walk and explore instead.

text: Guinea pigs often make a loud 'wheek' sound when they expect food.
explanation: Wheeking is a whistle-like call. Many guinea pigs wheek when they hear the fridge or a bag of vegetables.

text: Hay should make up most of a guinea pig's diet.
explanation: Fresh hay keeps their digestion working and their teeth healthy. Add fresh vegetables and some pellets.

text: Guinea pigs sleep all day and are active only at night.
explanation: Guinea pigs take many short naps and are active on and off during both the day and the night.

text: Guinea pigs are a kind of pig.
explanation: Guinea pigs are rodents, not pigs. They are also called cavies.

text: Guinea pigs are good climbers and enjoy high shelves.
explanation: Guinea pigs are poor climbers and can get hurt if they fall. Keep their home low, or use gentle ramps.

text: Guinea pigs need their nails trimmed regularly.
explanation: Their nails keep growing and can curl into the foot if they get too long. Most guinea pigs need a trim every few weeks.
